segments.en: And hopefully they're going to confirm the deal on Wednesday.

segments.en: So the first word for you guys today is photocopier.
segments.zh: 所以今天你们的第一个词是复印机。

segments.en: Now this is something that's very common in offices.
segments.zh: 现在这是办公室中非常普遍的事情。

segments.en: That's right, a photocopier, also known as a copy machine or just copier.
segments.zh: 没错，复印机，也称为复印机或只是复印机。

segments.en: Yeah this is something that you use to print on paper or to copy paper.
segments.zh: 是的，这是您用于在纸上打印或复印纸张的东西。

segments.en: So if I have a document but I want another copy of it, I put it on this machine and it will copy it and print it out.
segments.zh: 所以如果我有一份文件，但我想要它的另一个副本，我把它放在这台机器上，它会复制它并打印出来。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So those are the ways that you know this machine by this name.
segments.zh: 所以这些是你用这个名字知道这台机器的方式。

segments.en: Either photocopier, copy machine or just copier.

segments.en: Alright but after that we have a very interesting adjective.
segments.zh: 好吧，但在那之后我们有一个非常有趣的形容词。

segments.en: This is something that we use very often in spoken English.
segments.zh: 这是我们在英语口语中经常使用的东西。

segments.en: The phrase here Marco was I'm super busy but what does it mean to say you're super something?
segments.zh: 这里的短语 Marco 是我超级忙，但说你超级棒是什么意思？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So when we add the word super to an adjective, we mean that we're very, very, very busy, super busy.
segments.zh: 因此，当我们将超级单词添加到形容词中时，我们的意思是我们非常、非常、非常、非常忙碌。

segments.en: Alright so I'm super hungry.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我超级饿。

segments.en: That means you're very, very, very hungry.
segments.zh: 这意味着你非常、非常、非常饿。

segments.en: Alright or I'm super woman.
segments.zh: 好吧，或者我是超级女人。

segments.en: Also it means that you are very much a great woman.
segments.zh: 这也意味着你是一个非常伟大的女人。

segments.en: Alright like superman is very good at going fast and doing things and so he's super means great or exceptional.
segments.zh: 好吧，就像超人非常擅长快速和做事一样，所以他超级意味着伟大或非凡。

segments.en: So in this case I'm exceptionally busy.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我非常忙碌。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a contract, we know what this means.
segments.zh: 所以合同，我们知道这意味着什么。

segments.en: Yeah what is this?
segments.zh: 是的，这是什么？

segments.en: So a contract is a document and it's something that you have to have two or more groups for or two or more parties.
segments.zh: 所以合同是一份文件，它是你必须为或两个或多个方拥有两个或多个组的东西。

segments.en: So Marco between you and me, we could have a contract.
segments.zh: 所以马可在你我之间，我们可以有一份合同。

segments.en: It says that when we come to record, you will be respectful of me.
segments.zh: 它说当我们来记录时，你会尊重我。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And then we will both sign.
segments.zh: 然后我们都会签名。

segments.en: So it's kind of an agreement between two as you said or more people and but you are promising to respect the contract and to do what the contract says.
segments.zh: 所以这是你所说的或更多人之间的一种协议，但你承诺尊重合同并按照合同的规定去做。

segments.en: And if you don't do what the contract says, we have a special verb.
segments.zh: 如果你不按照合同所说的去做，我们有一个特殊的动词。

segments.en: We say you broke the contract.
segments.zh: 我们说你违反了合同。

segments.en: So to break, break a contract.
segments.zh: 所以要破产，破契。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So Jeremy was discussing the contract with Bill and they said they met the head of Lawsons.
segments.zh: 所以杰里米正在与比尔讨论合同，他们说他们会见了劳森斯的负责人。

segments.en: Now Lawsons is a company that we're just using for the dialogue.
segments.zh: 现在，Lawsons 是一家我们只是用于对话的公司。

segments.en: But what does it mean the head of this company?
segments.zh: 但是这家公司的负责人是什么意思？

segments.en: Okay if you think about the company as a body, the head is the top.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果您将公司视为一个机构，那么头就是顶部。

segments.en: And in this case that would be the president or the manager or the leader.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，那将是总裁、经理或领导者。

segments.en: It's the most important person.
segments.zh: 这是最重要的人。

segments.en: Okay so we can also use this in our offices for example the person in charge of marketing, the director of marketing.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们也可以在我们的办公室使用它，例如营销负责人，营销总监。

segments.en: We also call him the head of marketing.
segments.zh: 我们也称他为营销主管。

segments.en: Or the head of the sales division would be the manager of the sales team or whoever is most important in sales.
segments.zh: 或者销售部门的负责人将是销售团队的经理或销售人员中最重要的人。

segments.en: Another very common example I think is the president.
segments.zh: 我认为另一个非常常见的例子是总统。

segments.en: Many times they call him the head of state.

segments.en: Yeah the head of state.
segments.zh: 是的，国家元首。

segments.en: So you can have a dinner with many heads of state.

segments.en: And those could be kings or queens or presidents.

segments.en: Very good.

segments.en: Michelle says oh hi Jeremy please go ahead.

segments.en: Okay so Jeremy asks if she needs to use the photocopier and he said no Jeremy it's okay go ahead.

segments.en: This literally means you go ahead of me but in reality she's basically saying I can wait you go first.
segments.zh: 这字面意思是你领先于我，但实际上她基本上是在说我可以等你先走。

segments.en: So if you're going into a building and somebody opens the door before you and they say please go ahead.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您要进入建筑物并且有人在您面前打开门，他们说请继续。

segments.en: That means they'll hold the door and you can go inside first.

segments.en: So please go ahead.

segments.en: This is a very polite thing to do and if you're in line and you see someone is in a hurry you can say this to them please go ahead.
segments.zh: 这是一件非常有礼貌的事情，如果您排队并且您看到有人匆忙，您可以对他们说这话，请继续。

segments.zh: 因此，您有交易、协议或合同，但您要确保所有人都同意的事情是您确认。

segments.en: So this means you want to make sure it is actually going to happen.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着你要确保它真的会发生。

segments.en: And you can actually combine confirm with many different things like you can confirm your tickets to go to Italy or can we confirm those holidays before I make my bookings because I want to go to Italy.
segments.zh: 实际上，您可以将确认与许多不同的东西结合起来，例如您可以确认前往意大利的门票，或者我们可以在我预订之前确认这些假期，因为我想去意大利。

segments.en: Exactly.

segments.en: So you confirm something and then Jeremy said a very strange phrase here fingers crossed after talking about the deal.

segments.en: Okay so fingers crossed is an interesting phrase.
segments.zh: 好吧，手指交叉是一个有趣的短语。

segments.en: It doesn't mean okay now go cross your fingers but it's something we say to be superstitious because it means basically I hope so or hopefully because fingers crossed when you cross your fingers in many Anglo-American cultures you are saying that you hope something will happen.
segments.zh: 这并不意味着现在交叉手指，但这是我们所说的迷信，因为这意味着我基本上希望或希望，因为当你在许多英美文化中交叉手指时，你说你希望一些事情会发生。

segments.en: It's to bring good luck.

segments.en: So oh gosh I really hope it doesn't rain today.
